title: Photoelectron spectroscopy and Coulomb's law (AP); Orbitals and electron configuration
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: AS07#t3 term and clue written for the game; AS07#t1 term and clue written for the game; AS07#t2 term and clue written for the game; AS07#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AS04#N.6b, AS07#N.2, AS04#N.9b, AS07#N.5, AS04#N.11, AS07#N.7, AS04#N.12b, AS07#N.10, AS07#N.12.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Electronegativity
items.clue: How strongly a bonded atom attracts the shared pair.

items.label: Coulomb's law
items.clue: The force between two charges is proportional to q₁q₂/r².

items.label: Effective nuclear charge
items.clue: The net positive pull felt by a valence electron: roughly protons minus core electrons.

items.label: Photoelectron spectroscopy
items.clue: Fires X-rays or UV at gaseous atoms and measures the kinetic energy of what is ejected.

questions.stem: A student writes the electron configuration 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p⁶3d³ for a ground-state scandium atom, which has 21 electrons. Which statement correctly evaluates the student's configuration?

options.text: It is the ground state: subshells fill in order of shell number, so 3d is filled before 4s.
It is not the ground state: the third shell is full with 8 electrons, so the last three are 4s²4p¹.
It is not the ground state: 4s fills before 3d, so the last three electrons are 4s²3d¹.
It is not the ground state: d subshells begin in the fourth shell, so the last three are 4s²4d¹.

questions.explanation: After 3p, 4s fills, and the 21st electron enters 3d: …4s²3d¹.

questions.stem: Two particles with charges of +2 and −2 are separated by a distance d and attract each other with a force of magnitude F. Two other particles, with charges of +2 and −1, are separated by a distance of d/2. What is the magnitude of the force between the second pair of particles?
questions.explanation: Product of charges halved (4 → 2); 1/r² multiplied by 4. Force = (1/2)(4)F = 2.00F.

questions.stem: A ground-state iron atom has the electron configuration [Ar]4s²3d⁶. Which statement describes how a ground-state Fe²⁺ ion differs from the atom and gives its electron configuration?

options.text: Two electrons have been removed from the 3d subshell, giving [Ar]4s²3d⁴.
Two electrons have been added to the 3d subshell, giving [Ar]4s²3d⁸.
Two protons have been added to the nucleus; [Ar]4s²3d⁶ is left unchanged.
Two electrons have been removed from the 4s subshell, giving [Ar]3d⁶.

questions.explanation: Period 4 transition metal cations lose 4s electrons before any 3d.

questions.stem: A ground-state aluminum atom has the electron configuration 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p¹. How does the energy required to remove a 2p electron from the atom compare with the energy required to remove the 3p electron?

options.text: It is the same for both, since one nucleus attracts each of its electrons with equal force.
It is greater for the 3p electron, as an electron in a higher energy level needs more energy to leave.
It is smaller for a 2p electron, since six 2p electrons share an attraction that 3p has alone.
It is greater for a 2p electron, which is closer to the nucleus and shielded by fewer electrons.

questions.stem: An element has the ground-state electron configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 4s². The chemical properties of this element are most similar to those of which of the following elements?

options.text: He
Br
Mg
Ar

questions.explanation: This is calcium: two valence electrons (4s²). Magnesium has 3s², the same pattern one shell lower: group 2.

questions.stem: In a simple model, the force of attraction between the nucleus and a valence electron is proportional to q/r², where q is the net positive charge acting on the electron and r is the electron's average distance from the nucleus. For the valence electron of hypothetical atom Y, q is twice as great and r is twice as great as for the valence electron of hypothetical atom X. If the force on the valence electron of X is F, what is the force on the valence electron of Y?
Which statement best describes the electrons in a ground-state magnesium atom, 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s²?

options.text: They move on fixed circular paths, one path for each subshell, at set distances from the nucleus.
The two 3s electrons are core electrons, since the 3s subshell is full.
They occupy subshells of different energies; the two 3s electrons are the valence electrons.
All twelve are in the third shell, because magnesium is in period 3.

questions.explanation: The 3s electrons are, on average, farthest from the nucleus and need the least energy to remove.

questions.stem: Which description of the complete photoelectron spectrum of a ground-state silicon atom is correct?

options.text: Three peaks, one for each of the occupied shells
Five peaks, with the 2p peak tallest of all
Fourteen peaks, each of the same height
Five peaks, with the 1s peak the tallest

questions.explanation: Si is 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p². Five subshells, five peaks; heights 2 : 2 : 6 : 2 : 2, so 2p is tallest.

questions.stem: The complete photoelectron spectrum of an element has six peaks. From highest to lowest binding energy, their relative heights are 2, 2, 6, 2, 6 and 1. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The element is argon; the right-hand peak shows its outermost 3p electron.
The element is potassium; the right-hand peak is shortest because its electron needs the least energy.
The element is potassium; its 4s electron is farthest out and shielded by 18 core electrons.
The element is calcium; it has six occupied subshells, so its spectrum has six peaks.

questions.explanation: Heights add to 19 electrons: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 4s¹. The 4s electron is far from the nucleus with Zeff ≈ +1, so its peak is at the lowest binding energy.
